metadata.case_name: POON KWOK WING ERNEST v. AIRPORT AUTHORITY HONG KONG

plaintiff.occupation_before: Kerb Supervisor, responsible for directing traffic and enforcing the Bylaw of the Airport Authority Ordinance at the Chek Lap Kok Hong Kong International Airport

injuries.description: Injuries sustained from falling and rolling down escalator steps after sudden stoppage
source: Sometime between 1 and 2 p.m. on 9 April 2001, Mr. Poon was in the airport taking an escalator No. TIV2 down from level L5 to level L3. The escalator suddenly stopped, causing him to lose balance, fall and roll all the way down 20 odd steps to the bottom of the escalator and he, as a result, was injured.

injuries.description: Pre-existing degeneration of his back and corpulence
source: pre-existing degeneration of Mr. Poon’s back and his corpulence
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

manifestations.description: lose balance, fall and roll all the way down 20 odd steps to the bottom of the escalator
could not remain in a standing position for a long time

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities $55,000
